title.en: Compound collider mass, inertia and offset contract

summary: Build one rigid body from several parent-relative colliders while keeping dimensions, density, center of mass and inertia consistent with applied scale and the visual origin.
objective: An asymmetric compound body uses declared collider offsets and one mass policy; its reported center of mass and rotational response change predictably when a weighted collider moves, without visual/collision scale mismatch.
applies_when: One simulated part needs multiple primitive or convex colliders attached to one rigid body.
Visual origin, collider offsets or non-unit Blender object scale could change the center of mass or inertia.
intent_signals: compound collider with correct center of mass
example_prompts: Approximate a hammer with separate head and handle colliders and show its computed center of mass.
Build an asymmetric chassis collider whose mass and rotational response follow its scaled geometry.
negative_signals: Scaling only the Three.js mesh after collider dimensions were captured.
Adding explicit body mass properties while leaving nonzero collider density and assuming no contribution is added.
not_for: A deformable body whose mass distribution changes continuously.
Certification of a real product's inertia without measured geometry and density.

principles: Choose one mass policy: density/mass on attached colliders and solver recomputation, or explicit body mass properties with collider contributions deliberately zeroed. Do not unknowingly add both.
Each collider shape, rotation and translation is expressed relative to the rigid-body frame. The visual mesh, body origin and collider overlay must use the same unit/axis/scale conversion.

Treat scale as geometry input, not a late display adjustment. Apply or explicitly bake Blender object scale before computing primitive half-extents, offsets, mass, center of mass and inertia; reject zero, negative, nonfinite or unsupported shear.
implementation: Author named collider proxies in Blender or reviewed metadata, record their local transforms and intended densities, then convert once into the runtime body frame. Keep the render mesh independently detailed.

Create all colliders on one body using explicit dimensions and parent-relative transforms. After attachment, query mass, local/world center of mass and principal inertia where the binding permits; store expected totals for a small analytic fixture.

Reset restores collider geometry, offsets, density/mass policy, body pose and velocity together. Rebuild or recompute mass properties after an edit that represents physical shape or size. Cosmetic animation on a separate visual child may change its display scale only when it is explicitly declared nonphysical and never used to imply changed collision extent or mass.
observable_checks: Overlay each collider and its body-local axes on the visual mesh; after axis/unit conversion, named landmarks and bounds align within declared tolerance.
Two equal-density equal-volume colliders placed symmetrically yield a center of mass on the symmetry plane; increasing one density moves it toward that collider.
Removing or offsetting a collider changes reported mass properties and torque response. An explicit-mass fixture with zero-density colliders does not receive hidden collider mass.

creative_affordances: Collider proxies may resemble workshop jigs, translucent shells or schematic volumes while the visible object keeps its chosen style.
Center-of-mass and principal-axis markers can be optional inspection layers.
known_limits: Primitive or convex approximations may not reproduce the real body's mass distribution; declared density is a model input, not measured truth.
Triangle-mesh collider mass behavior and nonuniform scaling vary by engine and shape; this record requires explicit converted geometry rather than assuming universal support.
Authored guidance only; no Blender export, collider construction, mass query or torque test was run.

claims.statement: Rapier rigid-body mass properties comprise mass, angular inertia and center of mass. Attached colliders add shape-and-density-derived contributions, and explicit additional mass properties do not prevent those collider contributions unless collider densities are set to zero.
claims.scope: Rapier JavaScript mass-property model; it does not certify the fidelity of an authored collider approximation.

source_refs.locator: Mass/angular inertia/center-of-mass definitions; collider contribution; explicit additional properties and zero-density warning

claims.statement: Rapier collider descriptors accept shape dimensions, density, rotation and translation relative to an attached rigid body, and the body's mass properties are the sum of explicit body properties plus attached-collider properties.
claims.scope: Rapier JavaScript collider construction; unit and axis conversion from Blender remains application responsibility.

source_refs.locator: Primitive dimensions; setTranslation/setRotation relative to attached body; density and mass-properties sum

claims.statement: Blender's Apply operations transfer object transform coordinates to object data while visually retaining the object, and applying scale resets the object scale to one; modifiers and constraints may depend on the original transform, and armature application has additional limits.
claims.scope: Blender 4.5 object-transform authoring; deriving runtime collider values remains an authored conversion step.
